title: Factory and Abstract Factory
idea: A Factory pattern moves `new` behind one method that returns an interface. An Abstract Factory returns a whole family of related objects that must match.

analogy.text: You order a coffee by name; the counter decides which machine makes it. A hotel room kit hands you towels, slippers and soap that all match.
analogy.breaks: Java does not check that a kit's items match; the kit's author must.

points: Callers depend on the interface the factory returns, never on a concrete class.
Only the factory names concrete classes, so a new type edits one place.
An Abstract Factory is an interface with one creation method per product.
Each concrete factory builds one family, so one kit never mixes products.

steps.caption: `RegionKit` declares one method per product. `UkKit` and `IndiaKit` each implement all of them.
`main` is the only place that names a concrete kit. It passes it to `checkout`.
`checkout` holds a `RegionKit`. It cannot tell whether the kit is UK or India.
It asks the kit for a `TaxRule` and a `Receipt`. Both come from the same family.
One kit builds the whole set, so its tax rule and receipt always match.
A new region is one new kit class. `checkout` and the products' interfaces stay unchanged.

code.title: Factory
code.caption: The chapter 1 example used a `switch`; a registry `Map<String, Supplier<Notifier>>` adds types without editing the factory. GoF Factory Method instead lets subclasses override creation.

walk.text: The product interface: what every notifier can do.
Three concrete products. Only registrations refer to them by name.
The registry maps a channel name to a `Supplier` that builds a fresh notifier.
`register` adds a type at start-up; the factory's code stays unchanged.
`create` looks up the supplier and rejects unknown channels.
`main` registers push, then works with `Notifier` only.
An unsupported channel fails fast with a clear message.

code.title: Abstract Factory
code.caption: Each kit builds a tax rule and a receipt that belong together.

walk.text: Two product interfaces. Each has one method, so lambdas can implement them.
The abstract factory: one creation method per product in the family.
`UkKit` returns the UK tax rule and the matching UK receipt.
`IndiaKit` is a second family with the same shape.
`checkout` depends on `RegionKit` only and gets a matching pair.
The choice of family happens once, at the edge of the program.

pitfalls: Do not add a factory for a class with one implementation and no second coming.
Throw on unknown input in the factory; returning `null` moves the crash to the caller.
Adding a product to an Abstract Factory edits every concrete factory; keep families small.

quiz.q: What is the last line `NotifierFactoryDemo` prints?
options: PUSH to app: Order A-17 shipped
quiz.why: Nothing registered `fax`, so `create` throws `IllegalArgumentException` with the channel as its message. `main` catches it and prints that message.

takeaway: A factory hides which class you get; an Abstract Factory keeps families matched.
